text:
amanda: Heads-up — KadeshBank is hitting p99 token latency spikes on Dedicated pool-b-03 since ~08:00 UTC. They opened a ticket and want an ETA for a workaround. can eng-platform own triage? @raj @kevin

raj: on it. can you drop a sample request id + the exact pool name? also curious if this correlates with any recent rollouts.

amanda: sample req id: 01e3f9a2. pool: dedicated-prod-eu2/pool-b-03. pattern: timeouts (504) after 3 retries, increase in token processing time ~2x. no recent customer-facing rollouts from our side.

kevin: i'll take primary oncall for next 2h and run quick checks. first things i'll hit: pod health, autoscaler, node OOM, infra logs.

lina: looked at recent metrics: KV cache miss rate jumped ~40% around the same time and seq_len distribution shifted right. plausible that large input sizes are busting batching heuristics and inflating latencies. staged workaround: fallback routing to a smaller/quantized model variant to reduce per-token compute.

sam: product note — KadeshBank is on a strict SLA (p99 99.95%). they expect mitigation within ~4h. please be firm on customer comms.

raj: proposed immediate plan (owners):
- 0–30m (kevin): hot triage, disable continuous batching on pool-b-03, sanity-check node allocs.
- 30–90m (lina + raj): spin up canary with smol-quant model variant, route 20% traffic, observe p99 and error rate.
- 90–180m (raj): if canary acceptable, ramp routes and update customer; else roll back and prepare hotpatch.
Owners: kevin (oncall), lina (sre), raj (eng-platform). amanda to own customer comms.

amanda: copying customer support message: "we've identified degraded p99s for your dedicated pool, engineering is running mitigations now; expected initial improvement within 90 minutes, full resolution target 3–4 hours. we'll update every 30m."

kevin: running quick commands now:
```
kubectl get pods -n dedicated pool-b-03 -o wide
# pod list looks healthy but pod CPU at 95% on node gpu-eu2-07
kubectl logs pod/pool-b-03-7f6c -n dedicated | tail -n 50
# seeing repeated kv cache miss warnings and retry loops
```

deploy-bot: Deploy queued — canary-smol-quant v3 -> dedicated-prod-eu2/pool-b-03 (start 08:47 UTC).

lina: capacity check: eu2 has 2 spare gpus we can reserve for the canary for ~2h. i'll lock them and watch cache metrics. disabling batching should drop CPU but raise request count; watch autoscale.

raj: i'll open a short-runbook in the repo and add a checklist: toggle-batching -> canary -> monitor -> ramp. also creating PR to add a batching toggle flag in config (PR #4821).

sam: quick ask — kevin can you review PR #4821 once triage is stable? it's small and unblocks the toggle rollout.

kevin: will review after running the initial mitigation. quick findings: one node had a stuck kube-proxy restart loop; restarted it and CPU dipped 10%. still watching p99.

amanda: customer replied, appreciates quick action, asked for a follow-up when we have concrete numbers. i'll ping them at the 30m checkpoint.

lina: early signals: canary-smol-quant at 20% shows p99 down 35% and error rate halved. moving to 50% next if no regressions.

raj: golden — if 50% looks good at +30m we'll route full and close. assigning follow-ups: kevin (triage log dump + approve PR), lina (canary monitoring + capacity), raj (rollback/runbook + route changes), amanda (customer comms).

kevin: PR #4821 reviewed and approved. left one tiny nits but not blocking. :thumbsup:

sam: thanks — i'll coordinate the customer-facing summary after you confirm stable.

amanda: filed support update and set next update for +30m. thanks all.

raj: logging action items in tracker and will mark this thread once we've fully ramped and verified SLA. thanks team. :rocket:
